messages:
amanda: quick heads-up — we saw a routing mismatch in the TS canary (1.14.0) when the `route_hint` header is omitted. quota attribution flips to fallback pool instead of legacy-affinity pool. noticed on a small internal customer test. :frowning:

jia: ugh. any reproducible steps?

amanda: yes — minimal curl:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"input":"hi"}'``` vs with header:```curl -H "X-Route-Hint: pool=affinity-a" ...```
without header -> routed to `fallback-v2`, with header -> `affinity-a`. quota counters increment on fallback.

omar: that suggests the TS client changed default behavior for header injection or removed shim that fell back to the previous header name. did we change header normalization?

amanda: diff points to a runtime refactor: we now only send `X-Route-Hint` when `client.route` is set, previously the SDK preserved `route` metadata from env/config. so older deployments that relied on implicit route metadata lose it.

maria: can we detect impacted clients via telemetry? we need to know how many users rely on implicit injection before deciding a forced rollback.

kevin: propose add a short-term compat flag in SDK: `REDWOOD_SDK_LEGACY_ROUTE_INJECTION=1` that re-enables the old behavior. emit telemetry event `sdk.legacy_route_injection=true` on startup so console can chart it.

jia: agree. also add server-side metric `route_header_absent_count` and `fallback_pool_routed` so we can graph correlation.

omar: long-term we should standardize client metadata handling: explicit API for `client.routeHint()` and document deprecation. but the compat flag buys time.

amanda: for rollout, suggestion: 1) ship compat flag to TS now, 2) ship identical opt-in to Python/Go, 3) start 1% canary that enables flag for our internal QA org, 4) monitor new telemetry. anyone object?

maria: +1. I'll add a console dashboard tile that shows `sdk.legacy_route_injection` by SDK + version and a graph of `fallback_pool_routed` by org. we can also add an alert when fallback spikes >5% for an org.

kevin: we also need an interop test harness to validate header behavior across versions. I sketched a small matrix in the repo: run py/ts/go client versions against route-proxy v1/v2 and assert header presence and quota attribution. would like someone to own the test infra.

omar: I'll own the harness. will wire it to CI and a nightly matrix job. add a table of supported client versions we run against.

amanda: timeline? can we get the TS hotfix (compat flag) out today as a patch release and the Python/Go PRs merged tomorrow?

jia: TS patch ready, releasing now. dep-bot: releasing 1.14.1-canary.

deploy-bot: release started for package @redwood/sdk-ts@1.14.1-canary — canary -> 5 users target.

maria: I'll watch console dashboards + set alert.

kevin: once metrics look stable for 24h, we plan phased rollout and announce deprecation calendar for implicit injection (60 days). docs PR to follow.

amanda: also notify support and account execs for any customers affected by quota billing changes.

jia: one more: add a telemetry field `sdk.feature_flags` array so we can track future compat toggles without new events. e.g., `sdk.feature_flags=["legacy_route_injection"]`.

omar: good call. I'll include that in the harness and server acceptance tests.

amanda: thanks all. will follow up w/ PR links and a tiny how-to to opt-in for customers if they need immediate fix. :thumbsup:
